jobs.description:
Our Mission
At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.
Who We Are
In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!
We believe collaboration thrives in person. That’s why most of our teams work from the office full time, with flexibility when it’s needed. This model supports real-time problem-solving, stronger relationships, and the kind of precision that drives great outcomes.
Job Summary
Job Summary
As the Director of Ethics & Compliance (India), you will lead the design, implementation, and daily operation of our ethics and compliance program across India. You will own regional compliance risks, including anti-bribery, anti-corruption (ABAC), and trade compliance, acting as the primary compliance point of contact for business leaders. Occasionally supporting other regions like JAPAC and the Middle East, you will operate as a senior subject-matter expert ensuring our business adheres to the highest ethical standards.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the anti-bribery and anti-corruption (ABAC) program in India, managing risk assessments and third-party due diligence.
Monitor regulatory compliance requirements for India operations and track relevant legal developments affecting the business.
Cultivate proactive relationships with India Public Sector sales, commercial legal, and Public Policy teams on compliance matters.
Support India trade compliance matters, including import/export considerations and sanctions screening with global colleagues.
Serve as the primary regional resource for Code of Conduct questions, potential violations, and related internal investigations.
Design and deliver engaging compliance training and awareness programs tailored to the India business and workforce.
Conduct thorough compliance risk assessments and audits of business practices, policies, and third-party relationships within India.
Provide practical, risk-based compliance advice to business stakeholders on day-to-day operational questions and initiatives.
Support the intake, triage, and resolution of compliance concerns and whistleblower reports raised through reporting channels.
Provide ad hoc support on compliance projects in other territories, working alongside regional compliance officers.
Report on compliance program metrics, risks, and initiatives to the Head of Global Ethics and Compliance.
Maintain current knowledge of applicable anti-corruption, trade, and regulatory compliance laws, translating them into program updates.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
8+ years of relevant compliance experience in anti-bribery, regulatory, and/or trade compliance within a multinational corporate environment.
Bachelor's degree required.
Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or operating a compliance program, ideally within India and other emerging markets.
Working knowledge of Indian regulatory requirements and international anti-corruption frameworks like FCPA and UK Bribery Act.
Experience conducting or supporting internal investigations and third-party due diligence.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to provide pragmatic, risk-based guidance to business stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence without direct authority across a matrixed, global organization.
Willingness to support compliance matters in other territories and comfort working across diverse time zones and cultures.
Fluency in English and Hindi is required.
Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed for regional compliance activities.
Preferred Qualifications
A legal qualification is preferred but not required.
Proficiency in Kannada, Tamil, or other regional Indian languages is a plus.
Additional language skills, including Arabic, are highly advantageous.
Our Commitment
We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.
We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for all qualified individuals with a disability. If you require assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need, please contact us at accommodations@paloaltonetworks.com.
Palo Alto Networks is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity in our workplace, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or other legally protected characteristics.
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
Is role eligible for Immigration Sponsorship? No. Please note that we will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position.

jobs.description:
Make an impact at NTT Global Data Centers
Join NTT Global Data Centers and be part of a team that drives innovation and sustainability in the digital world. With over 150 data centers across more than 20 countries globally, we offer unparalleled opportunities to work on cutting-edge technology and transformative projects. Experience a collaborative, innovative, and inclusive workplace where your ideas are valued, and your growth is supported.
Your role at a glance
The Supply Chain Manager is accountable for the contracting, procurement, implementation, management, and day-to-day execution of the Construction Services equipment program supporting regional data center construction. Construction Services can include General Contractors, Architect/ Engineers, Commissioning, Controls, and related 3rd Party support services. The Supply Chain Manager will be responsible for the contracting and for the entire contract life cycle and contract administration. The Supply Chain Manager represents the Supply Chain organization and actively engages with the project team on all project strategy and project delivery activities to ensure supply chain strategies are aligned and meet all project build schedules, cost, design and capacity targets. This role requires an understanding of both construction project delivery and capital supply chain management in mission-critical environment.
What we are looking for
KEY responsibilities
Lead supplier relationship management and own the supply chain lifecycle for the respective Category, including sourcing, qualifying, RFx, evaluation, commercial negotiations, contract negotiations, award, change management support, management escalation, supplier business reviews, closeout, and claims mitigation/ management.
Lead the contracting life cycle from cradle to grave.
Work closely with regional and global contractor manager to execute the contracts- requirement gathering, drafting, negotiating conditions of contract, reviews and approvals, execution, deliverable tracking and close out.
Work with stakeholders and other supply chain teams for risk management and claims management.
Partner with project controls and finance to share procurement status, budget utilization, construction/ installation progress, ensuring transparency and cost accountability.
Manage impact of project specific design changes with suppliers and ensure fair and reasonable construction services and/or equipment pricing as a core business function related to contracts.
Anticipate issues in advance to prevent potential impacts, internally and externally to drive business decisions. This includes an in-depth understanding of the market environment and current events.
Monitor and populate key performance indicators (KPI’s) in support of the respective Category being managed. Measure performance against these KPIs and collaborate with stakeholders to evaluate supplier performance and drive continuous improvement.
Employ an analytics-based approach to support executive briefings and decision making along with capturing complex project data into program dashboard outputs.
Collaborate with stakeholders to identify demand, qualify, and execute selection of suppliers to deliver equipment and services to construction portfolio; support development of supplier allocation methodologies and regular business reviews with vendors to provide feedback and continuously improve supplier performance.
Be the first level escalation for all project construction and/or equipment concerns including vendor or overall supply chain issues (change orders, late deliveries, disputes, invoice accuracy, etc.); investigate, respond, and bring closure to suppliers, buyer’s agent, or other internal stakeholders.
Team with Critical Facilities Engineering and Operations groups to communicate extending lead times and obsolescence of components within supply chain activities. Be in the loop and ahead of upcoming or pending design changes which will impact equipment.
Support internal team(s) to renegotiate, extend options, renew, and discontinue supplier framework agreements as required and issue equipment orders under those framework agreements.
Ensure suppliers’ readiness and capability for all commissioning schedule and quality requirements.
Ensure supplier clarity, alignment, and ability to deliver on all project deliverables
KNOWLEDGE & ATTRIBUTES
Experience working in fast-paced, high-value capital projects.
Familiarity with international contracting standards and cross-border procurement.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS & CERTIFICATIONS
Master’s degree in relevant field of required qualification.
LEAN/Six Sigma Certification
PMP (Project Management Professional)
CPSM (Certified Professional in Supply Management)
REQUIRED EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, business administration, or relevant field.
Knowledge of FIDIC suite of contracts or other similar suite of industry contracts
Minimum of ten years of contracting, procurement and supply chain management required, preferably in a product/ category/ construction, and program management level.
Demonstrated success managing multimillion-dollar projects.
Who we are
As the third largest data center provider, we operate over 150 data centers in more than 20 countries and regions. We understand that every business – large and small – has its own unique needs and goals. We offer local-to-global data center expertise, aligned with our connected platform of AI-ready data centers to create solutions that enable our clients to seamlessly scale their digital businesses, anywhere and anytime.

jobs.description:
Make an impact at NTT Global Data Centers
Join NTT Global Data Centers and be part of a team that drives innovation and sustainability in the digital world. With over 150 data centers across more than 20 countries globally, we offer unparalleled opportunities to work on cutting-edge technology and transformative projects. Your role at a glance
The Director, Engineering Standards and Safety is a global role, that leads the global function that defines how engineering work is performed safely and consistently across data center operations. The role owns engineering standards, technical methods, operating boundaries, asset-acceptance criteria and the governance of technical deviations and risk acceptances. This director leads a multidisciplinary team covering electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life safety, and related engineering disciplines. The discipline standards engineers carry the primary research, evidence development, consultation and drafting workload. The Director sets priorities, challenges the evidence and retains final approval and governance authority. The function works with Field Engineering, Operations, Design, Construction, Commissioning, vendors and corporate safety teams to convert technical risk and operating experience into practical global requirements. Regional teams remain accountable for executing engineering work. Clear standards and safety controls help operating teams run critical facilities safely and efficiently, maintain reliable infrastructure, reduce avoidable environmental impact and provide consistent technical support to clients.
What we are looking for
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Set the global strategy, priorities and operating model for Engineering Standards & Safety.
Set the standards-development portfolio and research priorities, assign accountable discipline engineers and ensure work is proportionate to risk and business need.
Review and approve engineering standards, technical methods and analytical models developed through documented research and cross-functional consultation.
Ensure discipline engineers engage Field Engineering, site Operations, vendors and other experts, reconcile material input and maintain a traceable technical basis for each recommendation.
Define technical operating limits, system boundaries and escalation requirements for electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life-safety systems.
Establish engineering acceptance criteria for assets and systems entering operation, in partnership with Design, Construction, Commissioning and Operations.
Define validation frameworks for reliability analysis, energy analysis, technical-capacity analysis and control-strategy design.
Own the governance process for technical deviations and engineering risk acceptances, including approval authorities, evidence requirements, review periods and escalation thresholds.
Define engineering safety requirements for energized work, arc-flash risk, breaker coordination and other high-risk engineering activities.
Establish global control-system and alarm philosophy, including control-sequence principles, setpoint governance, alarm requirements, point naming, tagging and metadata standards.
Establish fire and life-safety engineering requirements and assurance methods in partnership with corporate safety, regional teams and authorities having jurisdiction.
Monitor adoption of standards, identify systemic compliance gaps and sponsor corrective actions without assuming regional execution ownership.
Ensure standards reflect operating experience, incident learning, regulatory requirements, recognized industry practices and changes in technology.
Chair or sponsor governance forums that resolve cross-region technical questions, approve material exceptions and assign clear decision ownership.
Build and lead a high-performing global team through workforce planning, hiring, coaching, performance management and succession planning.
Communicate engineering requirements, material risks and decisions to senior leaders in clear technical and business terms.
Manage the function's priorities, resources, external technical support and budget in line with approved business plans.
ROLE AND DECISION SCOPEKE
Owns
Global engineering standards, methods and technical governance for operating facilities.
Technical operating boundaries and asset-acceptance criteria.
Engineering-safety requirements within the function's remit.
Control and alarm philosophy and related naming, tagging and metadata standards.
The engineering deviation and risk-acceptance framework.
Assurance methods for adoption and continued suitability of standards.
Approves
New and materially revised global engineering standards.
Standards-development priorities and the evidence required before a proposal enters formal approval.
Technical deviations and engineering risk acceptances within delegated authority.
Validation methods used to demonstrate compliance with engineering requirements.
Function priorities, resources and technical-governance forums.
Recommends or Escalates
Material engineering risks that exceed delegated authority or risk tolerance.
Investment or remediation needed to close systemic standards and safety gaps.
Changes to enterprise policy, design standards or operational practices owned by other functions.
Regulatory, safety or technical matters requiring executive or legal review.
Outside This Role's Scope
Regional execution of engineering studies, projects or routine engineering work.
Real-time facility control, uptime management and operational response.
Incident command or coordination.
Definition of performance KPIs owned by Optimization & Analytics.
Maintenance scheduling, work-order management or local procedure approval.
Physical meter, asset or network maintenance.
KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS
Regional Field Engineering directors and discipline managers
Site and regional Operations leadership
Reliability, Optimization & Analytics and Technical Capacity leaders
Design, Construction, Commissioning and Capital Projects
Corporate and regional Health, Safety, Security and Environment teams
Sustainability, Legal, Risk, Finance and Procurement
Equipment manufacturers, engineering consultants and insurers
Regulators, standards bodies and authorities having jurisdiction
KNOWLEDGE & ATTRIBUTES
Deep knowledge of engineering principles used in mission-critical or data center facilities, with strong working knowledge across electrical, mechanical and controls systems.
Strong knowledge of engineering risk management, technical assurance, change control and standards governance.
Knowledge of energized-work safety, arc-flash analysis, short-circuit and breaker-coordination principles.
Knowledge of control sequences, building-management systems, electrical power-management systems, alarm philosophy and operational technology interfaces.
Working knowledge of fire detection, suppression and life-safety engineering requirements.
Ability to translate codes, regulations, operating experience and technical analysis into clear, usable global standards.
Ability to evaluate complex technical evidence, make risk-based decisions and explain the basis for those decisions.
Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams across regions and cultures.
Strong organizational leadership, workforce planning, coaching and performance-management skills.
Ability to influence senior stakeholders and resolve ownership or technical conflicts without relying on direct authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including standards, executive briefings and technical decision records.
Ability to balance safety, reliability, operability, efficiency, cost and long-term asset health.
ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS, CERTIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
Required
Bachelor's degree in electrical, mechanical, controls, fire-protection or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant education and experience where company policy permits.
At least 12 years of progressive engineering experience in mission-critical facilities, industrial infrastructure, utilities or a comparable high-availability environment.
At least 5 years of experience leading engineering teams, technical authorities or enterprise standards programs.
Demonstrated experience developing or governing engineering standards, technical methods, safety requirements or formal risk-acceptance processes.
Experience working with data center or other mission-critical electrical, cooling and controls infrastructure.
Experience operating across multiple regions or business units and influencing senior technical and operational stakeholders.
Preferred
Master's degree in engineering, engineering management or a related field.
Professional Engineer, Chartered Engineer or equivalent professional registration.
Experience with relevant NFPA, IEEE, IEC, ISO, ASHRAE or equivalent regional standards.
Formal training or certification in electrical safety, functional safety, fire protection, risk management or management systems.
Experience participating in industry standards bodies, technical committees or regulatory engagement.
MEASURES OF SUCCESS
Engineering standards are current, clear, usable and adopted consistently across regions.
Material engineering and safety risks are identified, governed and escalated within defined timeframes.
Technical deviations and risk acceptances have complete evidence, clear ownership and effective expiration or review controls.
Regions have fewer conflicting interpretations of operating limits, acceptance criteria and engineering methods.
Systemic assurance findings result in timely, durable corrective action by the accountable execution teams.
The function maintains the technical capability, succession coverage and stakeholder trust needed to perform its global mandate.
WORK CONDITIONS & OTHER REQUIREMENTS
This is a global role with regular collaboration across time zones.
International and domestic travel is expected, typically up to 25%.
The role may occasionally support urgent technical or safety matters outside normal business hours.
Work includes office or home-office activity and visits to operating or construction-stage data centers.
Site visits may involve noise, heat, electrical and mechanical equipment, stairs or ladders, and required personal protective equipment.
Employment classification, work arrangement and any additional physical requirements will follow the requirements of the hiring location. Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable law.
Compensation Pay Range

Engineering Manager, Production Engineering - Observability
An overview of this role
You'll lead the globally distributed Observability team. The team builds and operates the metrics, logging, alerting, and capacity planning platforms that GitLab engineers use to understand GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated. You'll help determine how the team collects, stores, queries, and acts on telemetry, balancing reliable signals with scale and cost.
In your first year, you'll guide improvements to Prometheus-based metrics pipelines, log ingestion and retention, alerting driven by service-level objectives (SLOs), and capacity forecasting. You'll work with Site Reliability Engineering, Product Engineering, and other Infrastructure Platforms teams to make it easier for engineers to observe the services they own. You'll also take part in incident response and help keep the team's on-call work sustainable.
What you’ll do
Lead, hire, onboard, and develop a distributed engineering team working asynchronously.
Set priorities with Site Reliability Engineering, Product Engineering, and GitLab Dedicated teams, and help the team deliver observability services iteratively.
Own the reliability, scalability, and cost of the team's metrics, logging, alerting, and capacity planning platforms.
Reduce noisy or missing alerts and telemetry gaps, and use SLOs, error budgets, and self-service instrumentation to help engineers maintain the health of their services.
Guide technical decisions about time-series storage, high-cardinality metrics, log pipelines, and distributed tracing.
Participate in the Incident Manager On Call (IMOC) rotation, coordinating the response to high-severity incidents affecting GitLab.com.
Keep the team's on-call rotation sustainable through coverage across time zones, useful runbooks, better alerts, and follow-through on post-incident actions.
Use AI tools and agents to support engineering workflows and incident triage, reviewing their output while engineers retain responsibility for decisions.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you’ll bring
Experience leading an observability, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering team operating at scale, including supporting people in a distributed, asynchronous environment.
Technical knowledge of metrics systems such as Prometheus and long-term storage, logging platforms such as Elasticsearch or cloud-native services, and alerting design.
Experience using SLOs, error budgets, and capacity forecasts to make reliability and investment decisions.
Experience operating a large software-as-a-service platform and investigating production issues such as telemetry gaps, ingestion limits, or noisy and missing alerts.
Experience participating in and improving production on-call rotations, including incident coordination and balancing operational load with project work.
The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to engineering partners and other stakeholders.
Experience using AI tools or agents in engineering or management work; you can describe how you would apply them to operational problems such as incident triage.
We welcome different paths into this role, whether through practical experience, formal study, or transferable skills. If the work interests you, please apply even if you don't meet every qualification.

We're part of Production Engineering within Infrastructure Platforms and work asynchronously across regions. Our tools include Tamland, the capacity forecasting tool. We bring lessons from operating GitLab's production systems back into the platforms we build.

Ownership: You'll take features from requirements through delivery and follow-up; your code will run on a platform used by millions of users.
Learning and Growth : You’ll work alongside your engineering team, who treat code review and design review as a learning loop rather than a gate — one of the fastest ways to grow your engineering judgment.

Own and Ship Features: Design, implement, test, and ship backend features and improvements with minimal guidance, working in Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern languages.
Build for Production: Write maintainable, secure, observable, and performant code. Design and maintain APIs, background jobs, integrations, and bounded service functionality, and work with data models, migrations, indexes, and query behavior.
Test and Review: Add and improve automated coverage — unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end where appropriate — and review others’ code for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and operational risk.
Operate What You Build: Investigate build, test, deployment, and runtime failures at the feature boundary, identify technical debt and propose practical improvements, and take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

Feature Ownership: The ability to take a feature from clarification through delivery and follow-up, working independently while seeking input at the right time.
Practical Judgment: Sound instincts about security, reliability, performance, maintainability, and operational risk, plus an understanding of modular backend boundaries and the consequences of coupling.
Clear Communication: Strong written communication and effective collaboration in a remote, asynchronous environment.
AI Fluency: Practical experience with AI coding tools, including the ability to review and correct what they generate.

Production Go services, APIs, concurrency, profiling, or gRPC.
Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, CI/CD, or cloud deployment.
Rust, particularly for systems, security, performance, or platform work.
PostgreSQL, schema evolution, caching, queues, messaging, or event-driven workflows.
Observability using metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerts.
Contributing to a modular monolith, bounded context, shared component, or independently operated service.

GATE will become the foundation for token issuance, validation, and identity services across GitLab.com multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS), Self-Managed, Dedicated, and air-gapped environments. Your work will affect core components that customers, users, and GitLab teams rely on.
Some of our projects include:
Building GATE as the centralized service for token issuance and validation
Consolidating tokens and migrating authentication paths out of the Rails monolith
Building passkeys and passwordless authentication
Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI
Improving service accounts and secure automation
Enhancing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) capabilities for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO)
What you'll do
Shape the roadmap for GATE and GitLab's authentication services with the team.
Design and implement token issuance, validation, and identity services in Go and Ruby across the Rails monolith and GATE, including new authentication mechanisms such as Workload Identity Federation.
Migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models.
Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation.
Strengthen security for users and organizations through access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.
Define and improve standards for style, maintainability, and engineering practices in a high-scale environment, and advocate for them through code review.
Communicate publicly about GitLab initiatives, projects, and contributions from people not working for GitLab Inc. Reflect GitLab's values in these communications.
Ship moderately sized features and improvements with moderate guidance and support from other team members, and collaborate on larger projects, including the build-out of GATE.
Participate in the maintainer trainee program at your own comfortable pace while working toward becoming a project maintainer.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Professional experience with Go and/or Ruby in scaling or mission-critical SaaS products.
Familiarity with authentication and authorization technologies or techniques, such as OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SSO, SCIM, LDAP, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), role-based access control (RBAC), or identity and access management (IAM).
Knowledge of token systems, cryptographic signing, and key management.
Experience building or contributing to a service from concept to production, including proposal, discussion, and execution.
Proficiency in written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate complex problems and solutions clearly in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.
Experience diagnosing, preventing, and resolving performance and optimization problems.
Experience working in an iterative software development process, managing your work effectively, staying organized, and following through on priorities.

Authentication is the first impression a new customer has when they configure a new GitLab instance. We aim to make it as seamless as possible, from that first login to onboarding users and managing security rules for their instance in a secure, flexible, and scalable way.

This is a technical leadership role that combines deep backend expertise, systems judgment, product judgment, and influence across organizational boundaries. You will work with Product, Frontend, Infrastructure, Security, Data, Engineering Managers, and engineers across product groups, bringing subject matter expertise, and you will do it without relying on formal authority.
Why you’ll love this role
Leverage: Your work multiplies across teams. The platforms, standards, and architectural decisions you lead determine how quickly everyone else can ship.
Genuinely Hard Problems: You’ll lead the modernization of a large monolith toward modular, reusable, appropriately independent systems — at the scale of a platform used by millions of users.
Influence Without Bureaucracy: You’ll shape technical direction across teams through clear written proposals and decision records, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform roadmap and investment trade-offs.
Frontier AI Work: You’ll lead adoption of AI-assisted and agentic engineering workflows and define the review, quality, security, and privacy guardrails that make them safe to rely on.
Autonomy: You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.

Lead Cross-Cutting Initiatives: Lead the technical design and delivery of large backend initiatives that span teams, and identify and remove systemic bottlenecks across product and infrastructure groups.
Own Architecture Strategy: Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture. Lead modernization of the monolith and legacy backends toward modular, reusable, and appropriately independently operated systems — while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.
Set the Standards: Define and improve standards for APIs, contracts, compatibility, schema evolution, testing, security, performance, observability, operability, and maintainability — plus the build, test, deploy, release, rollback, and production-readiness practices needed to operate modular features safely.
Establish Shared Patterns: Create the patterns for dependency management, data ownership, eventing, failure isolation, service maturity, and operational documentation. Establish Go service patterns and Kubernetes operating practices where they matter to our production estate, and guide Rust adoption where it solves a real systems, security, performance, or supply-chain problem.
Own What You Build in Production: Take part in on-call and incident response for the systems your teams own, act as a technical escalation point during complex incidents, and turn what you learn into architectural and operational improvements that prevent recurrence.
Influence and Partner: Shape technical direction across teams without formal authority, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform-level roadmap decisions and investment trade-offs.
Grow Engineers: Mentor Senior and Intermediate engineers, shepherd technical debt reduction and reusable patterns that improve throughput, and raise the technical capability of the wider team.
Lead AI Adoption: Lead team-level adoption of AI-assisted and agentic workflows, including the quality, security, privacy, and operational guardrails, and help engineers direct, validate, reject, and course-correct agent output.
On-Call Support: Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

Cross-Team Technical Leadership: A sustained record of technical leadership across more than one team or a broad product area.
Deep Architecture Experience: Deep backend architecture and production experience in complex applications, services, or platforms, including scaling or governing APIs, service platforms, data systems, modular monoliths, or shared backend components.

Mentorship: Experience mentoring engineers and shaping standards through code review, documentation, and example.
Agentic AI Leadership: Production experience with AI-assisted or agentic engineering workflows, including the ability to evaluate and improve how a team adopts them.

Go services and APIs at scale.
Kubernetes and cloud-native operations, including deployment, scaling, observability, rollback, and production readiness.
Rust adoption or production ownership for systems, security, performance, or platform components.
Ruby/Rails modularization and large-monolith modernization.
PostgreSQL scaling, data partitioning, queues, messaging, or distributed systems.

Some examples of the projects you could work on:

Creating and maintaining deployment packages for GitLab, such as Helm Charts and omnibus-gitlab
Building and operating Dedicated GitLab instances integrated with cloud-native services (e.g., GCP, AWS)

Deploying and managing microservices on Kubernetes clusters at scale
Enhancing GitLab’s observability stack (e.g., Prometheus, ELK) to support proactive monitoring and incident response

Debug & Resolve Production Issues: Troubleshoot issues across Kubernetes clusters, cloud services, and GitLab apps—identifying root causes of failed deployments, crash loops, and scheduling conflicts to ensure service continuity.
Automate Operations at Scale: Replace manual workflows with infrastructure-as-code solutions, including automated version upgrades, configuration rollouts, and provisioning pipelines that operate reliably across all tenants.
Monitor & Predict Capacity: Build observability systems that detect bottlenecks, predict usage trends, and optimize resource consumption using tools like Prometheus, ELK, and Grafana.
Respond & Lead During Incidents: Lead incident response and postmortem efforts, applying technical depth to resolve issues and establish operational standards that reduce future risk.
Architect & Collaborate: Influence architectural decisions around automation, scalability, and operational excellence. Partner with engineering teams to improve automation, platform resilience, and production-readiness.

Production-Scale Experience: Proven ability to operate and troubleshoot production workloads across multiple tenants or environments. Deep understanding of how distributed systems fail at scale and how to build in resilience.
Terraform & IaC Mastery: Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, including workspace strategies, state management, and automation patterns that scale. Comfortable solving state isolation issues and building reliable, reusable infrastructure code. Experience with Ansible and templating tools like Jsonnet is a plus.

An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.
Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.
We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.
What you'll do
Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

An overview of this role
As a Staff Software Engineer on GitLab's Authentication team, you'll be the technical lead for how every user, application, token, and automated agent proves who it is on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.
We're an OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for millions of users. We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest.
Our projects include:
OAuth across Cells: Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells
Global identities: One user identity that works across organizations and cells
Token consolidation: Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith
Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads: OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes
What you'll do
Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services.
Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags.
Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.
Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers.
Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes.
Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents.
Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group.
Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code.
Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation.
Working knowledge of SAML 2.0 single sign-on and enterprise identity integration (LDAP, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or similar).
Strong production experience in Ruby on Rails or Go, willingness to work in both, and experience with careful refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and backward-compatible migrations in large, long-lived codebases.
A security mindset. You think about token theft, replay, revocation, and blast radius before you think about elegance.
Experience with multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) systems, including data isolation and performance under high request volume.
Clear, concise written English and comfort working in an all-remote, asynchronous company.
Optional experience: authentication libraries (Doorkeeper, Devise, or OmniAuth), passkeys or multi-factor authentication, workload identity, gateways or policy engines, AI agent authentication, or multi-region architectures. Contributions to identity standards or open source identity projects are also welcome.
About the team
The Authentication group is part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. We own sign-in, single sign-on, OAuth, and personal and service tokens. Our work touches every GitLab customer, and much of it is on the critical path for Cells and for GitLab's AI agent platform.

As an Applied AI Engineer at GitLab, you'll build and deploy AI-powered solutions for GitLab's own teams. You'll join Enterprise AI in the CIO organization, reporting to the Senior Director, Enterprise AI. This is a hands-on engineering role: you'll write production code and partner with senior engineers and internal business stakeholders to solve problems and deliver measurable outcomes. Your focus is GitLab's internal operations, rather than customer implementations or development of the GitLab product.
Building fast matters, and we want engineers who ship. But speed without understanding the problem leads to the wrong solution shipped quickly. You'll partner with senior engineers and stakeholders to understand the real problem first: how work moves across teams, where the real constraint lives, and whether AI is the right intervention. From there, you'll take ownership of the build and deployment, combining strong engineering skills with curiosity about the business systems you're improving.
Your initial focus will span GitLab's own Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support teams, where you'll embed AI solutions into the systems and workflows they use every day. This role offers the opportunity to grow as an engineer while shaping how GitLab team members work, in a remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.
What you'll do
Contribute to problem diagnosis alongside the team. Engage with stakeholders to understand the real constraint before reaching for a solution, and be willing to flag when AI isn't the right answer.
Own the build and deployment of AI solutions, from technical design through implementation, deployment, and iteration. Partner with senior engineers on discovery and scoping.
Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value.
Build solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Track flow, adoption, and ROI metrics defined for the work.
Integrate AI capabilities into GitLab's internal business systems and workflows using APIs, orchestration tools, and modern AI platforms, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, where appropriate. The right tool wins, whether that's custom code, a platform, or a well-crafted prompt.
Be Customer Zero: use GitLab's AI products in our own internal workflows, assess how they perform in practice, and share feedback with R&D to help improve them.
Partner with stakeholders to translate requirements into working solutions. Ask good questions, surface assumptions, and align with the team on outcomes before jumping to implementation.
Track success against defined business metrics, flow metrics, and feedback loops that make performance visible and actionable.
Contribute to documentation and reusable patterns that help the team scale its impact.
What you'll bring
A Technologist at Heart - Genuinely invested in technology, the foundational and the cutting-edge in equal measure. You're as energized by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. You reach for the simplest solution that solves the problem well, rather than forcing new technology when proven approaches would do. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them.
Competent, Confident Coding Skills - You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently.AI & LLM Technical Depth - Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. Practical, hands-on experience with modern AI technologies, specifically:
Prompt engineering as a core discipline: designing effective system prompts, managing context windows, structuring multi-turn interactions, evaluating output quality, and iterating systematically on prompt design.
Model selection and cost-performance trade-offs: developing judgment on when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, when RAG is the right architecture versus expanding the context window, and how to think about capability versus cost.
Agentic architecture patterns: tool use, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop designs, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and production-grade reliability patterns.
Practical fluency across the LLM ecosystem: hands-on experience with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source alternatives, and growing judgment about which to reach for and when.
AI Safety & Risk Awareness - You think critically about how the solutions you build could be exploited, misused, or produce unintended consequences. You know how to design appropriate guardrails (input validation, output filtering, access controls, prompt injection defenses, and data leakage prevention) and you treat these as first-class engineering concerns.
Curiosity About Flow & Constraints - Comfortable engaging with workflow maps, end-to-end process diagrams, and constraint analysis. You instinctively ask "what's actually blocking flow here?" before asking "what model should I use?" You don't need to be the one leading the diagnosis yet, but you should be eager to learn and contribute.
Business System Awareness - Familiarity with the landscape of enterprise business systems: CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (Marketo), support platforms (Zendesk), integration and orchestration tools (Workato), AI platforms (Relevance AI), and enterprise search and knowledge tools (Glean). You don't need deep experience with all of these, but you should understand what they do, be willing to learn how they fit together, and be ready to build with and across them.
Cross-Functional Communication - Comfortable having conversations with stakeholders across diverse domains, willing to invest in understanding their unique needs, and able to translate between technical and business language.
Ownership Mindset - Track record of taking scoped initiatives from design through delivery. Comfortable operating with some ambiguity, and knows when to push forward independently versus when to ask for guidance.
Product Mindset - Ability to scope MVPs, prioritize ruthlessly, and deliver iteratively. In addition, consider adoption, user experience, and business outcomes.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with GitLab platform and CI/CD workflows
Background in solutions engineering, solutions architecture, consulting, or other stakeholder-facing technical roles, combining strong engineering skills with stakeholder engagement, solution design, and root cause analysis. Experience personally building and shipping production-quality solutions is especially relevant.
Familiarity with value stream mapping, flow metrics, or Theory of Constraints thinking
Experience with low-code/no-code orchestration tools (n8n, Make, Workato) alongside custom development
Previous startup or high-growth company experience
About the team
You will join the Enterprise Technology & AI team in the CIO organization. We build and improve the internal systems and workflows that help GitLab team members make decisions, operate at scale, and do their best work.
We believe the best AI solutions start with understanding the system, not the technology. We value people who think in constraints and flow, who build with conviction, and who never stop learning. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous setting, guided by GitLab's operating principles of Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, built on a Culture of Excellence.

You are not waiting for someone to hand you a perfect onboarding plan. You ask questions, you read documentation, you look at logs, and you figure it out. When you write a script, you think about whether someone else will be able to run it six months from now. You care about the details because you have seen what happens when a small mistake makes it into a release. At Synopsys, you will work on standard cell libraries that power chip designs across the industry, and the validation work you do will matter from day one.
What You'll Be Doing
Create and validate library views across multiple formats and technology nodes to support diverse design and signoff requirements.
Develop, validate, and package library deliverables for internal teams and external customer releases, ensuring completeness and correctness.
Generate and validate Apache Power Library models including SPIPROF, Current, CDEV, and PWCDEV for power integrity and signoff flows.
Execute comprehensive quality checks across library builds, APL models, and release packages to catch issues before they reach downstream users.
Debug and resolve complex issues in characterization flows, APL model generation, build validation, and release processes.
Build and maintain Python and Shell automation to improve validation coverage, reduce manual effort, and increase release velocity.
Collaborate with characterization, design, CAD, QA, and release teams to align on requirements, troubleshoot blockers, and deliver on schedule.
The Impact You Will Have
Enable design teams and customers to meet tape-out schedules by delivering high-quality, validated library deliverables on time.
Reduce downstream design issues by catching library and APL model inconsistencies early through rigorous validation.
Accelerate release cycles by building automation that replaces manual validation steps and improves flow reliability.
Improve power signoff accuracy by delivering validated SPIPROF, CDEV, and PWCDEV models that reflect real silicon behavior.
Drive quality improvements across the library development pipeline by identifying gaps in validation coverage and closing them.
Solve customer-reported library and APL issues quickly, reducing support escalations and maintaining customer trust.
Contribute to continuous improvement efforts that make validation flows faster, more robust, and easier to maintain.
What You'll Need
Bachelor's in Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
Basic knowledge of CMOS/FINFET/GAA technology, Digital Electronics and Logic Design, Combinational and Sequential Circuits.
Solid debugging skills across complex multi-step flows involving characterization, model generation, and release processes.
Ability to work across teams and communicate technical issues clearly to design, CAD, QA, and release stakeholders.
Self-motivated, curious, eager to learn, strong ownership mindset, ability to work with geographically distributed teams.
Who You Are
You can trace a library issue from a customer report back through the build flow, characterization run, and source data without getting lost.

jobs.title: Financial & Prudential Reporting, Associate
jobs.description:
About this role
India controllers and Financial & Prudential Reporting, Associate
Business Unit Overview:
The mission of Finance is to be a trusted advisor to the business, safeguarding BlackRock's financial integrity while enabling sustainable growth through exceptional financial stewardship, rigorous controls, and insightful decision support.
The Financial & Prudential Reporting (FPR) team within APAC Controllers is responsible for the financial stewardship of BlackRock's APAC legal entities, ensuring the integrity of financial reporting, regulatory compliance, and a strong internal control environment. Through a regional hub operating model, the team partners closely with stakeholders across Finance, Technology, and broader business functions to deliver high-quality reporting, support strategic initiatives, and drive continuous process improvement.
The Gurgaon-based India FPR team is a key contributor to APAC's controllership agenda, supporting complex accounting, regulatory reporting, audits, transformation initiatives, and technology-enabled process enhancements across multiple jurisdictions.
Job Purpose:
The Associate in the India Controller’s and Financial & Prudential Reporting team will lead financial accounting and compliance reporting for entities in the India Jurisdiction). The role is responsible for the timely and accurate delivery of financial reporting. Additionally, the role will provide end-to-end accounting and reporting operations support including reporting processes governance, and audit engagement for the India entities, ensuring compliance with Indian Accounting Standards, local regulatory requirements, IFRS/US GAAP and internal control standards.
The successful candidate will exhibit strong accounting & reporting skills, demonstrate deep expertise in accounting and financial reporting processes, and have a proven track record of driving process improvement and excellence. This role requires the ability to foster a high-performing culture, ensure operational excellence, and deliver measurable business outcomes aligned with organizational objectives.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead and support legal entity accounting, financial close, statutory and regulatory reporting activities for India entities, ensuring the timely, accurate, and complete delivery of financial information and regulatory submissions.
Prepare, review, and submit statutory and regulatory financial statements and surveys in compliance with Ind AS, IFRS, US GAAP and local GAAP, the Companies Act, RBI, MCA and other applicable requirements.
Coordinate internal and external audit activities for India entities, including the timely delivery of audit support, management of audit requests, resolution of audit queries, and tracking of audit observations and remediation actions.
Support and maintain a robust internal control environment aligned to SOX/ICoFAR and corporate policies; monitor key controls, remediate deficiencies, and reduce operational risk.
Monitor developments in accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and reporting obligations, assess their impact on the business, and support implementation of necessary changes across reporting and control processes.
Drive standardization, documentation, and automation of reporting processes, partnering with Technology teams to enhance data quality, improve efficiency and strengthen controls.
Partner with regional controllers and stakeholders across Corporate Accounting, Finance Operations, Tax, Treasury, Accounting Policy, Technology, and other finance functions to resolve accounting, reporting, and operational matters and support business initiatives.
Drive or participate in finance transformation, migration, and integration projects and champion risk-based prioritization to deliver sustainable outcomes.
Skills and Qualifications:
Chartered Accountant with experience in global asset management preferred
5+ years of experience in financial services industry
Strong technical knowledge of IND AS, the Companies Act, MCA / RBI Compliances, US GAAP and IFRS.
Ability to manage multiple deliverables in a deadline-driven environment while maintaining accuracy and quality.
Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communications skills, including active listening and the ability to articulate complex issues to a variety of audiences.
Proven experience in process optimization and automation; familiarity with Oracle ERP/General ledger, consolidation and reporting tools preferred.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, challenging environment while maintaining a focus on quality.
Sound understanding of modern technologies, Artificial intelligence tools and Industrial development.
Our benefits
To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.
Our hybrid work model
BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
Guidance on AI use for candidates
At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.
About BlackRock
At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.
This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.
To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.
BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, family status, gender identity, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected attributes at law.

jobs.description:
Voyager (94001), India, Bangalore, Karnātaka
Distinguished AI Engineer
At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.
Team Description:
The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. Our Generative AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products by composing powerful, safe and explainable AI capabilities such as agentic workflows, and shared services such as guardrails, observability and evals coupled with foundational model power of open-weight and proprietary frontier models. The team is also delivering capabilities on top of the platform to optimize the software development life-cycle to dramatically enhance developer productivity and model-development life cycle to improve time-to-market of machine learning models.
In this role, you will:
Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, similarity search, guardrails, evals engine, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, Nemo Guardrails, PyTorch, and more.
Invent and introduce state-of-the-art LLM optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systems.
Devise novel context generation techniques that optimize cost / quality trade-offs.
Design and implement capabilities for automated monitoring, anomaly detection and RCA for multi-turn and headless agentic applications.
You will collaborate with lines of businesses to design and implement high value agentic applications
Finally you will coach and evangelize, mentoring Staff, Principal and Senior engineers, authoring technical design documents and blogs and representing Capital One at Tier1 AI conferences.
The Ideal Candidate:
Passion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in production.
You adapt quickly and thrive on bringing clarity to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and digging deep to uncover the root of problems and can articulate your findings concisely with clarity. You have the courage to share new ideas even when they are unproven.
You are deeply Technical. You possess a strong foundation in engineering and mathematics, and your expertise in hardware, software, and AI enable you to see and exploit optimization opportunities that others miss.
You are a resilient trail blazer who can forge new paths to achieve business goals when the route is unknown.
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering
At least 6 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies
At least 8 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, or Java
Preferred Qualifications:
10+ years of experience deploying scalable and responsible solutions on cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or equivalent private cloud)
4+ years of experience architecting, designing, developing, integrating, delivering, and supporting complex AI systems
6+ years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies (e.g. LLM Inference, Similarity Search and VectorDBs, Guardrails, Memory) using Python, C++, C#, Java, or Golang
2+ years of experience with Agentic frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen etc.)
2+ years of experience leading GenAI or LLM-Powered application architectures in production
2+ years of experience developing and applying state-of-the-art techniques for optimizing training and inference software to improve hardware utilization, latency, throughput, and cost
2+ years of experience with Observability and Evals for agentic applications
Passion for staying abreast of the latest AI research and AI systems, and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor multiple engineering teams and influence cross-functional stakeholders up to the VP level
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex AI concepts to peers
Master’s or Ph.D in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, especially in AI/ML areas.

Industrial System Analytics (ISA) is a product group that develops cloud analytic solutions using GCP tools and techniques. This Technical Program Manager role is ideal for a technically fluent program leader who wants to drive delivery across a portfolio of strategic analytic solutions. You will collaborate with Business Customers, Product Management, Engineering, DP&E and IT to convert business goals into analytic solutions, working with Balanced Product Teams that embrace lean and agile practices, automated testing, and CI/CD.
This is a hybrid role suited for someone who can move fluidly between writing PRDs and prototyping a model, between running sprint planning and reviewing training data quality. You'll own the product vision, roadmap, and delivery for AI-driven features while staying technically credible with the engineering and data science teams you work alongside.
Key Responsibilities
Product Management
Define and own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for AI/ML-powered products and features.
Translate business problems and customer needs into clear product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Manage the end-to-end product lifecycle: discovery, prioritization, development, launch, and post-launch iteration.
Run agile ceremonies (sprint planning, backlog grooming, retrospectives) and manage execution using Jira, Confluence, and similar tools.
Balance and manage multiple concurrent product workstreams/portfolios, prioritizing across competing stakeholder demands.
Define and track success metrics/KPIs (model performance, adoption, latency, cost-per-inference, business impact).
Partner cross-functionally with engineering, data science, design, legal/compliance, and business stakeholders.
Communicate roadmap, progress, and trade-offs clearly to leadership and stakeholders.
Hands-On Technical / AI-ML
Directly contribute to prototyping, fine-tuning, evaluating, and iterating on LLMs and other ML models (e.g., prompt engineering, RAG pipelines, fine-tuning, embeddings).
Collaborate closely with engineers/data scientists on data pipelines, model architecture trade-offs, and deployment strategy (MLOps).
Evaluate build-vs-buy decisions for foundation models, vector databases, and AI infrastructure tooling.
Stay current on the AI/LLM landscape (new model releases, techniques, regulatory/ethical considerations) and translate emerging capabilities into product opportunities.
Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) or B.Tech — Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics, or related discipline.
5 to 7 years of total professional experience, including 3 years in Product Management (AI/ML or data-driven products preferred).
Demonstrated hands-on experience building, fine-tuning, or deploying LLMs — not just managing engineers who do so (e.g., portfolio, GitHub, published work, or specific project examples).
Practical knowledge of Python and common ML/AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face) or LLM tooling (Google ADK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, vector DBs).

Excellent stakeholder management, written, and verbal communication skills — able to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences and vice versa.

Certifications in Product Management (CSPO, PMP) and/or AI/ML certifications are an added advantage.

Shipped AI/LLM-powered features that measurably improve user outcomes and business KPIs.
A well-managed, transparent roadmap and backlog across multiple concurrent initiatives.
Strong trust from both business stakeholders (for product judgment) and technical teams (for technical credibility).
Continuous improvement of model quality metrics through direct hands-on involvement, not just delegation.

Senior Platform Engineer (Associate Architect) – SAP AI Foundation
Location: Bangalore (Whitefield)
Job Family: Platform Engineering
Where You'll Belong
SAP AI Product & Engineering is a key driver of the Autonomous Enterprise, bringing AI capabilities to enterprise applications and helping customers unlock the value of their business data. Our foundational products—including SAP Generative AI Hub, AI Core, and AI Launchpad—enable application developers to embed AI into enterprise solutions.
We value engineers who combine strong hands-on implementation skills with sound architectural judgment, proactively address risks, and take accountability for sustainable solutions. Grow as a senior engineer and emerging architectural leader while helping shape the next generation of enterprise AI platforms at SAP.
What you'll build
As a Senior Platform Engineer (Associate Architect), you will take end-to-end ownership of critical components within SAP AI Foundation. You will design, develop, test, deploy, and operate cloud-native platform services that power enterprise AI workloads.
This is a hands-on senior engineering role combining deep implementation expertise with architectural responsibility. You will independently deliver complex engineering capabilities, influence technical direction across components, and drive solutions that improve platform scalability, reliability, security, and operational efficiency.
You will work closely with architects, product management, and globally distributed engineering teams to translate product requirements into robust technical solutions. You will also mentor engineers and contribute to the evolution of platform architecture while remaining actively involved in design and implementation.
Own platform components across design, development, testing, deployment, and production operations.
Independently deliver complex features with high engineering quality, transparency, and accountability.
Contribute to the design and evolution of scalable, secure, and maintainable distributed systems. Evaluate technology choices, integration patterns, architectural trade-offs, and long-term platform evolution.
Identify reusable design patterns and opportunities to simplify system complexity and reduce technical debt.
Integrate platform capabilities with SAP BTP, SAP AI Core, SAP HANA and relevant enterprise services.
Develop and operate microservices using Python, Java, or Go. Work with Kubernetes, containers, distributed systems, and cloud-native infrastructure.
Improve observability through structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, dashboards, and actionable alerts.
Strengthen CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, deployment automation, and developer productivity.
Apply secure-by-design principles across authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, network security, encryption, and sensitive-data handling.
Follow engineering standards for code quality, automated testing, vulnerability management, and security.
Mentor junior engineers through code reviews, design discussions, and technical guidance.
Collaborate with product management, architects, engineers, and distributed engineering teams.
What you’ll bring
A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. 10+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, or backend systems development.
Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, design patterns, and software design principles.
Deep understanding of distributed systems, microservices, API design, and cloud-native architectures.
Strong proficiency in Python, Java, or Go, with demonstrated ability to design and implement production-quality software.
Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Docker, containers, and cloud-native deployment patterns.
Experience building, debugging, and operating distributed services in production environments.
Solid understanding of CI/CD, automated testing, and software delivery practices.
Practical knowledge of observability, production troubleshooting, reliability engineering, and performance optimization.
Strong security fundamentals, including authentication, authorization, data protection, and secure software development.
Ability to drive technical decisions, evaluate architectural trade-offs, and communicate design proposals clearly.
A strong ownership mindset, excellent problem-solving skills, and the ability to collaborate across globally distributed teams.
Experience with SAP BTP, SAP AI Core, SAP HANA, or other enterprise cloud platforms is an advantage.
Additional Information:
