jobs.title: Field Applications Engineer, Design and Verification
jobs.description:
Verification Applications Engineer
Customer Success Engineer, Verification
Technical Applications Engineer, EDA
Field Applications Engineer, Design and Verification
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent time in verification environments where the difference between a clean tape-out and a schedule slip often comes down to how fast someone can debug a simulation failure at 2am. You know your way around SystemVerilog testbenches, and you have stared at waveforms long enough to spot the signal toggle that should not be there. You are the person teammates come to when something breaks in a way that does not make sense yet.
Working directly with customers energizes you. You do not just want to hand over a solution, you want to understand the problem first, ask the right questions, and propose something that actually fits their flow. You are comfortable on a call with a design team in another timezone, walking through a debug scenario or explaining why a coverage hole matters.
You learn fast. New methodologies, new tools, new customer designs, you adapt without needing six months of ramp time.
You understand that successful chip development extends beyond simulation and debug. Exposure to RTL quality and design sign-off methodologies such as Lint, Clock Domain Crossing (CDC), and Reset Domain Crossing (RDC) analysis is valuable, and you appreciate how these technologies complement verification flows in achieving tape-out readiness. You are also curious about emerging AI technologies and how AI-assisted and agentic solutions can improve engineering productivity and customer success.
At Synopsys, you will work with verification engineers who are solving real problems on real chips, and the solutions you help deliver will directly affect whether those chips make it to production on time.
What You'll Be Doing
Support customers using Synopsys verification and design sign-off tools such as VCS, Verdi, and VC SpyGlass, diagnosing simulation issues, debug challenges, coverage gaps, RTL quality concerns, and Lint/CDC/RDC issues in their design flows
Work with customers on RTL sign-off methodologies including Lint, Clock Domain Crossing (CDC), and Reset Domain Crossing (RDC) analysis, helping identify root causes and improve design quality before tape-out
Analyze customer testbenches and design environments to identify root causes of verification failures and propose technical solutions that fit their methodology
Work on verification challenges involving SystemVerilog, UVM, low power verification, and coverage-driven workflows across diverse customer projects
Collaborate with Synopsys R&D teams to escalate complex issues, contribute to product improvements, and bring customer feedback into the development cycle
Build scripts in Tcl, Python, or Perl to automate workflows, replicate customer issues, demonstrate best practices, and improve engineering productivity through automation and AI-assisted workflows
Guide customers through tape-out cycles, helping them stay on schedule by resolving verification bottlenecks quickly and effectively
Travel occasionally to customer sites for onsite technical engagements, training, or critical project support
The Impact You Will Have
You will directly reduce time to tape-out for customers by solving verification issues that would otherwise stall their schedules for days or weeks
Your technical guidance will help design teams adopt better debug and coverage practices, improving the quality and efficiency of their verification environments
You will influence product roadmaps by surfacing real customer pain points to R&D, ensuring future releases address the problems that matter most
The solutions you deliver will enable customers to verify complex, multi-million gate designs with confidence, reducing costly respins
You will help customers adopt advanced verification methodologies and low power techniques that directly impact chip performance and power efficiency
You will help customers improve RTL quality and sign-off readiness by addressing lint, CDC, and RDC challenges early in the design cycle, reducing silicon risk and improving tape-out confidence
You will help customers adopt innovative automation and AI-assisted engineering workflows that improve productivity and accelerate problem resolution
Your work will strengthen customer relationships and trust in Synopsys tools, contributing to long-term partnerships and renewals
You will build a knowledge base of customer use cases and solutions that benefits the broader applications engineering team across global locations
What You'll Need
Bachelor's degree in Electronics Engineering or related field with 2+ years of experience in verification, digital design, or design sign-off, or a Master's degree in Electronics
Strong fundamentals in digital design and hands-on experience with Verilog or VHDL
Working knowledge of SystemVerilog and dynamic simulation concepts, including testbench development and debug
Proficiency in UNIX or Linux environments and scripting with Tcl, Python, or Perl
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, you will be interfacing directly with customers to understand their challenges and explain technical solutions clearly
Experience or exposure to RTL sign-off methodologies including Lint, Clock Domain Crossing (CDC), and Reset Domain Crossing (RDC) analysis is highly desirable
Experience with Synopsys tools such as VCS, Verdi, or VC SpyGlass is a strong plus
Exposure to UVM, coverage-driven verification, low power verification flows, or RTL sign-off methodologies is advantageous
Awareness of Generative AI technologies, AI-powered engineering workflows, or agentic solutions is an added advantage
Who You Are
You can take a vague customer complaint like 'simulation is slow' or 'design checking reports thousands of CDC violations' and turn it into a specific diagnosis with a proposed fix
You are comfortable working across timezones and cultures, partnering with engineers in different locations without losing clarity or momentum
You stay organized when juggling multiple customer cases at once, and you know which issue needs attention first based on impact and urgency
You do not wait for perfect information to start solving a problem, you dig in, replicate the issue, and work iteratively toward a solution
You are comfortable learning and applying new technologies, including AI-assisted engineering tools and agentic solutions, to improve efficiency and solve customer challenges
You are willing to travel occasionally for customer visits, training sessions, or critical project support when the situation calls for it
You bring an innovative mindset to recurring problems, always looking for ways to automate, simplify, or improve the process for the next time
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will join the Customer Success Group in Hyderabad, a team focused on building strong technical partnerships with customers and helping them solve high-value verification challenges. You will work closely with domain experts across global locations, including R&D, sales, and other applications engineers, in a collaborative environment where knowledge sharing and continuous learning are part of the culture. The team supports customers throughout their tape-out schedules, and your role will directly contribute to their success in verifying complex chip designs on time.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Procurement Strategy & Insights Manager
jobs.description:
Job Title: Procurement Strategy & Insights Manager
Country Location and Worksite Details: India - UniOps Bangalore Centre.
Earlier this year, Unilever announced an agreement to combine its Foods business with McCormick & Company, creating a scaled global flavour powerhouse. The proposed combination would bring together iconic Foods brands, including Hellmann’s and Knorr, with McCormick’s portfolio to create a global leader across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by strong retail and foodservice platforms. McCormick brings more than 135 years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, with completion estimated for mid-2027.
Business Context and Main Purpose of the Job
This role exists to own delivery of Strategy and Insights workstreams that enable Procurement to improve process excellence, AI and digital enablement, data-driven decision-making and transformation adoption across markets, business groups and portfolios. The role leads transformation programmes in an agile manner, working closely with Procurement leadership, Finance, digital enablement teams, market and business group stakeholders to create measurable step-change in procurement performance. Through insight, analytics, process discipline and structured storytelling, the role converts procurement, supplier, market, spend, savings, risk and value-chain data into actionable recommendations and scalable adoption roadmaps.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Own delivery of Strategy and Insights workstreams that enable Procurement to improve process excellence, AI and digital enablement, data-driven decision-making and transformation adoption across markets, business groups and portfolios.
Lead transformation programmes in an agile manner, aligning Procurement leadership, Finance, digital enablement teams, market and business group stakeholders around clear outcomes, adoption plans and measurable value.
Develop and govern insights, dashboards, analytics and performance routines that translate procurement, supplier, market, spend, savings, risk and value-chain data into actionable recommendations.
Drive adoption of AI, automation, digital procurement tools, standardised processes, playbooks and analytics-enabled ways of working to improve speed, quality, consistency and value creation.
Identify, scale and embed value opportunities and best practices across procurement teams through price transparency, ZBB, buying performance, competitor benchmarking, cost modelling, value-chain diagnostics, learning interventions and future-fit upskilling.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
University degree in Procurement, Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Analytics, Data Science, Engineering, Technology or a related discipline, with 7–10 years of procurement, supply-chain, strategy, analytics, consulting, process excellence, business transformation or digital enablement experience.
Strong understanding of procurement strategy, operating processes, sourcing performance, supplier markets, spend analytics, savings delivery, value-chain analysis and transformation adoption.
Strong capability in process excellence, AI and digital procurement tools, automation, dashboarding, data architecture, insight generation, cost modelling, benchmarking and performance management.
Proven experience leading transformation workstreams, agile delivery, stakeholder adoption, hypothesis testing, structured problem solving, capability building and cross-functional change.
Strong analytical, storytelling, senior stakeholder, communication and influencing skills.
Strong command of written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly with senior stakeholders in a global business environment.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Relevant transformation, digital, analytics or procurement qualification.
Experience working virtually across markets, business groups, portfolio teams, Procurement Finance, digital teams, supplier operations and external insight partners.
Hindi and/or other foreign language capability, particularly languages relevant to regional or global stakeholder engagement, would be advantageous.
Experience building procurement capability through playbooks, communities, learning interventions, governance standards and future-fit upskilling would also be advantageous.

Unilever embraces diversity and encourages applicants from all walks of life! This means giving full and fair consideration to all applicants and continuing development of all employees regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership, and pregnancy and maternity.

Have a deep understanding of the requirements and functionalities of high-performance networking software with at least 15 years of experience in leading software product delivery.
Have an outstanding grasp of computer architecture and operating systems and in-depth knowledge of data structures, algorithms and multi-core programming.
Be motivated to accept a variety of responsibilities in contributing to Arm’s success and capable of aspiring and mentoring junior members of the team.

Experience with open-source software contribution process and CI/CD pipelines.

jobs.title: Software Functional Safety and Cybersecurity Manager
jobs.description:
JOB OVERVIEW
Join Arm’s CE Quality and Compliance team as a Software Functional Safety and Cybersecurity Manager. You’ll support automotive and robotics software programmes through development, assessment and release, working with engineering and business teams on products such as software self-test libraries.
You’ll help teams apply practical, scalable approaches to functional safety, automotive cybersecurity and quality, aligning software development with industry standards and customer requirements.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Support automotive and robotics software programmes from development through to certification.
Work with engineering teams to align development practices with industry standards and customer requirements.
Prepare teams for external assessments and lead internal audits and reviews.
Help teams prepare compliance evidence, safety documentation and responses to assessors.
Establish process improvements, training, corrective actions and engineering best practices across the software organisation.
Contribute to safety-readiness initiatives across automotive, robotics, AI and industrial domains.
Work with engineering and assurance teams on process improvement and automation, including data analytics and AI tools that support human judgement on safety and security.
REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
Software development experience in safety-critical industries.
Practical knowledge of ISO 26262, ISO/SAE 21434, Automotive SPICE, IEC 61508 or similar standards.
Experience supporting engineering teams with compliance, audits and process improvement, including functional safety or cybersecurity assessments and their work products.
Ability to communicate, solve problems and work with stakeholders across technical and organisational boundaries.
NICE-TO-HAVE SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
Experience with processor safety mechanisms, such as software self-test libraries or software-based diagnostics.
Experience working with external assessors or certification bodies.
Familiarity with open-source or embedded software supply chains and their safety and security implications.
IN RETURN

jobs.title: Principal SOC Modeling Engineer
jobs.description:
Principal SOC Modeling Engineer
The Software (CE-SW) group is responsible for developing and improving the software ecosystem around Arm's next generation architectures and systems. This means working with processors and other hardware technology not yet available to the public. You will join a team of Software Engineers who share a passion for leaving their mark on the future of computing.
We are looking for software engineers to join the Arm Fast Models team responsible for building high-performance software models of Arm-based systems. These models enable early software development, architecture exploration, and system validation before silicon is available. Members of the modelling team transform hardware designs and specifications into high-performance software representations of hardware systems and components.
In this role, you will develop functional models of CPUs, system IP, and complete Arm's reference platforms using C++ and SystemC, working closely with hardware and software teams across Arm.
If you are similarly passionate about innovative technologies, then we would love to hear from you!
Key responsibilities include:
Develop, test, and maintain high-performance functional models of Arm system-level IP using C++ and SystemC.
Build virtual platforms representing complete Arm’s reference platforms to enable early firmware, OS, and application development before silicon availability.
Collaborate with hardware architects and RTL designers to understand IP specifications and ensure accurate behavioral modelling.
Work with open-source and software engineering teams to enable software bring-up on virtual platforms and diagnose system-level issues.
Integrate multiple IP models to create scalable system-level simulations.
Participate in planning and execution of development roadmaps, working with project managers and global engineering teams.
Required Skills and Experience
Minimum 15-20 years of proven experience.
Strong C/C++ programming skills with experience in developing large-scale software systems.
Experience in SoC or IP modelling using C++, SystemC, or TLM.
Good understanding of computer architecture, microarchitecture, and SoC design concepts.
Experience with software development practices including debugging, testing, and performance optimization.
Experience using version control systems such as Git/Gerrit.
Understanding of RISC-based architectures and familiarity with CPU instruction sets.
Ability to work effectively independently and within distributed global teams.
Strong interpersonal skills, excellent written and spoken English.
Nice to Have
Experience with Programmer’s View (PV) modelling and SystemC TLM-2.0 methodologies.
Knowledge of Arm architecture or Arm system IP (CPU, interconnects, GIC, SMMU, etc.).
Experience building SoC virtual platforms or full-system simulators.
Background in low-level software, firmware, bare-metal programming, or device drivers.
Experience in supporting to large-scale multi-site software projects.
Why Join Us
Work on modern virtual platforms used across the Arm ecosystem.
Experience with hardware validation labs and test farms.
Collaborate with world-class engineers across global Arm teams.
A clear path for career progression, with scope to evolve into technical leadership or management roles.

jobs.title: Engineer – Emulation/FPGA
jobs.description:
Job Overview
Help develop, bring up and deliver emulation and FPGA prototyping platforms for Arm’s next-generation compute subsystems and systems on chip (SoCs). In this hands-on role, you’ll turn RTL designs into validated hardware acceleration platforms that support early system validation and hardware-software co-development. You’ll work with design, verification, software, validation, infrastructure and electronic design automation (EDA) teams.
Responsibilities
Develop and bring up emulation and FPGA models for subsystem and SoC designs, including RTL integration, compilation, synthesis, partitioning, deployment and debug.
Deliver functional, stable and reproducible hardware acceleration platforms for engineering teams.
Support system bring-up, including boot flows, firmware loading, memory, interconnect and high-speed interfaces such as PCIe and CXL.
Investigate and resolve issues across RTL, firmware, software, tools and infrastructure, including simulation-emulation mismatches and system-level failures.
Improve platform performance and efficiency through build optimisation, automation, regression and debug improvements.
Develop reusable methodologies and flows, and work with EDA vendors and engineering teams to investigate tool issues and improve reliability and resource use.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience with an emulation or FPGA platform, such as Synopsys ZeBu or HAPS, Siemens Veloce or proFPGA, or Cadence Palladium.
Experience compiling, implementing, bringing up and debugging subsystem or SoC designs on hardware acceleration platforms.
Understanding of SystemVerilog or Verilog, RTL development, synthesis, partitioning, place-and-route and timing analysis.
Understanding of CPU and SoC architecture, boot flows, memory systems, interconnects and system integration, with the ability to investigate hardware and RTL issues collaboratively.
Nice-to-Have Skills and Experience
Experience with large SoC or multi-die/chiplet emulation and FPGA prototyping.
Familiarity with Arm CPU architecture, CMN/interconnect, GIC or SMMU.
Knowledge of interfaces such as PCIe, CXL, UCIe, Ethernet, DDR, LPDDR or HBM.
Experience with firmware, bare-metal programming or system boot.
Familiarity with hybrid emulation and simulation, transactors or FPGA implementation flows.
Experience with performance or power analysis, CI/CD, scripting, automation, Linux, EDA debugging tools or post-silicon validation.
In Return
You’ll work on next-generation compute subsystems and SoCs, helping teams begin system validation and software development earlier. You’ll collaborate across engineering disciplines and contribute to reusable flows and methodologies used across projects.
Additional Information
Please note that no relocation package is available for this role.

Works with contractors and consultants to review quality assurance for all system expansions, corrections, and upgrades.

Ensures data centre operates at maximum operational efficiency, including analysing existing operating conditions, recommending new technologies and improving overall efficiency, and cost reduction.

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

We are looking for problem solvers, innovators, and analytical thinkers who challenge the status quo. If you are an experienced technologist passionate about the intersection of cloud architecture, big data, machine learning workloads, and financial accountability, this role is for you.
As a Senior FinOps Engineer, you will serve as the technical backbone and subject matter expert for cloud financial operations across our global engineering organization. This role bridges deep cloud infrastructure mechanics with data engineering, algorithm design, and business economics. You will architect automated reporting pipelines, develop unit-cost metrics, govern procurement and operational policies, introduce FinOps practices for AI workloads, and partner closely with engineering squads, platform teams, and finance leaders to foster a culture of cost-aware engineering.
Key Responsibilities
1. Cloud Cost Visibility, Data Analytics & Anomaly Detection
Manage, curate, and normalize end-to-end cloud cost and usage datasets, ensuring high data fidelity, consistency, and standardized governance across multi-cloud environments.
Define, build, and maintain automated cost, usage, and efficiency dashboards using Apache Superset, supported by SQL and data extraction pipelines.
Design and deploy automated anomaly detection algorithms, statistical models, and alerting mechanisms to detect spending spikes, runaway workloads, and unexpected cost regressions in near real time.
Benchmark, track, and report on cloud consumption, forecast variance, unit economics, and realized savings to engineering teams and leadership.
Implement and refine tagging governance, business cost-allocation models, and unit economics metrics, such as cost per customer, cost per query, or cost per pipeline run.
2. Architecture, Automation & Spend Optimization
Own and optimize cloud financial management platforms for reporting, cost optimization, and performance measurement. Our environment includes Cloudability, PointFive, ProsperOps, and Larridin; experience with comparable platforms is welcome.
Design, build, and maintain automation workflows and scripts to identify and reclaim idle, underutilized, or orphaned resources, including compute instances, unattached volumes/IPs, outdated snapshots, and development/test environments.
Lead enterprise-wide commitment strategies across AWS, Azure, and GCP, managing portfolio coverage, risk, and utilization for Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and applicable provider-specific commitments.
Partner with software, platform, and SRE teams to analyze utilization telemetry, implement rightsizing recommendations, and optimize compute and storage resources.
3. FinOps for AI & Emerging Technologies
Introduce and establish FinOps frameworks tailored to AI, ML training pipelines, and LLM inference workloads.
Establish Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and Return on Investment (ROI) models for AI infrastructure, including GPU clusters, vector databases, model hosting endpoints, and third-party AI APIs.
Collaborate with AI/ML engineering teams to evaluate model inference performance against operational costs, improving token efficiency and hardware utilization.
4. Governance, Procurement & Cross-Functional Alignment
Establish and enforce cloud cost and operational policies across accounts, subscriptions, regions, and resource configurations.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Memory Design
jobs.description:
Staff Memory Design Engineer
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent years in the analog and mixed-signal trenches, designing memory circuits that have to work across voltage corners, temperature extremes, and process variations without a second chance. You know that an SRAM bitcell is not just six transistors on a page, it is a tradeoff between read stability, write margin, leakage, and area, and you have made those calls enough times to know which knob to turn when a design is not closing.
You think in terms of transistor-level behavior, not just simulation results. When a memory fails at a corner, you do not just re-run SPICE, you go back to the schematic, check your layout parasitics, and figure out what actually broke. You have worked closely with layout teams, and you understand that a good floorplan saves you three weeks of iteration later.
You are comfortable owning a memory block from architecture through tapeout. You can sit with a compiler team and explain why your bitcell needs a specific routing constraint, then turn around and review a layout with a physical design engineer without losing context. At Synopsys, you will design embedded memories that ship in our IP portfolio and power chips across the industry.
What You'll Be Doing
Design and develop embedded CMOS memories including single-port SRAM, dual-port SRAM, register files, and ROM for Synopsys IP products
Own circuit architecture and transistor-level implementation for ultra-high-speed, ultra-low-power, or high-density memory configurations
Perform schematic entry, SPICE simulation, layout planning, and supervise physical layout execution through to final verification
Develop and verify bitcells, define layout rules, and drive layout design and parasitic extraction closure with the physical design team
Interface with CAD teams to integrate memory designs into compiler automation flows and generate EDA models for customer use
Collaborate with frontend engineers to define and validate full verification flows including timing, power, and functional models
Mentor junior engineers and lead technical aspects of memory design projects from concept to delivery
The Impact You Will Have
Your memory designs will ship as part of Synopsys IP offerings used by semiconductor companies worldwide in high-volume production chips
The bitcells and architectures you develop will define performance, power, and area benchmarks for next-generation embedded memory IP
Your layout planning and verification rigor will reduce tapeout risk and speed time to market for memory compiler releases
The automation flows you help define will enable faster, more reliable memory generation for customers across process nodes
Your technical mentorship will build design capability within the team and raise the quality bar for future memory products
The tradeoffs you make between speed, power, and density will directly influence customer adoption and competitiveness in the IP market
Your collaboration with CAD and frontend teams will improve tooling, models, and verification coverage across the memory IP portfolio
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related technical field
Deep hands-on experience with CMOS memory circuit design including SRAM, register files, or ROM
Proficiency with circuit simulation tools such as HSPICE, Spectre, or similar SPICE-based simulators
Strong understanding of memory layout design, parasitic extraction, and layout verification tools like Calibre or Assura
Scripting capability in C-Shell, Perl, or similar languages; experience with C++ or JavaScript is a plus
Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and mentor junior engineers through complex design challenges
Experience working with memory compiler flows, EDA model generation, or design automation is a strong plus
Who You Are
You can look at a bitcell schematic and immediately spot a read stability issue or a leakage path without running a full simulation
You know how to work with layout designers, not just hand off a schematic and hope for the best, you review floorplans, flag routing issues, and iterate together
You are comfortable making technical tradeoffs in ambiguity, choosing between a faster access time and lower leakage when the spec does not give you both
You can explain a circuit-level design decision to a compiler engineer or a product manager in terms they understand without oversimplifying the engineering
You stay organized across multiple design blocks, verification runs, and layout reviews without losing track of what is blocking tapeout
You take ownership, if a memory fails characterization, you do not wait for someone else to debug it, you dig in and figure out what went wrong
The Team You'll Be Part Of
Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

Keep it up. Monitoring, alerting, and frontline incident response that catch problems before customers do.
Make it stable. Root-cause analysis of recurring failures, plus closing security and compliance findings.
Run it well. Cataloging supported assets, tracking run costs, and keeping practices consistent.
Make it easy to get help. One clear way to ask for support, backed by automation and AI agents.

You'll manage escalations across teams and time zones, act as a frontline responder who swarms incidents and knows when to pull in reliability engineers, own root-cause analysis through to resolution, and design monitoring that gives early warning. Escalation Management & Incident Response
Own escalations on cases, intake, and investigations across teams and time zones: set priority, route to the right engineering, SRE, or vendor owner, drive them to closure, and keep stakeholders informed.
Run follow-the-sun handoffs so escalations keep moving between Mexico City, Dublin, and Hyderabad without losing context.
Track escalation trends (volume, repeat causes, time to engage, time to resolve), and bring them to leads and platform engineering to drive fixes.
Be the escalation point for Tier-2 analysts on complex cases and investigations.
Be a frontline responder in incidents: connect first, assess impact, and use judgment on when to pull in Site Reliability Engineers (SREs). Manage the case, intake, and stakeholder communication workstream alongside Incident Command. SREs own incident resolution.
Meet individual and team lifecycle SLAs: First Response Time (FRT), Next Response Time (NRT), and Average Resolution Time (ART), and case satisfaction (CSAT) targets while keeping backlog health. You are measured against the same targets as the team.
Help L7 refine the intake and investigation lifecycle SLAs: mentor Systems Analysts on hitting them, and raise challenges where targets, routing, or processes make them hard to meet.
Spot patterns in SLA misses and satisfaction feedback, and bring recommended fixes to the L7 and the team.
Problem Management & RCA Ownership
Own root-cause analysis and resolution for application bugs and recurring failures, and close RCAs with verified fixes.
Troubleshoot complex declarative and low-code issues, and recommend code-level fixes to engineering partners.
Prioritize technical debt against the backlog to improve stability, and recommend fixes.
Reliability & Observability
Design and implement proactive monitors, alerts, and automations for platform health.
Contribute to design reviews and operating-model improvements (for example Operational Readiness practices).
Use automation and AI to reduce manual work and move the team toward self-healing operations.
Platform Administration & Enhancement
Deliver complex declarative solutions (Flows, validation rules, permission models) and manage enhancement projects from inception through support transition.
Own complex access and role-hierarchy design, bulk data loads and migrations, and sandbox management.
Reliably handle standard administration so the team can focus on higher-value work.
Process Engineering, SOPs & Support Reference Manuals
Own process engineering for your platform area: templates, process design, capture, and lifecycle (create, review, update, retire) of lightweight SOPs and Support Reference Manuals (SRMs). This is process design, not technical writing.
Request SRM inputs from Platform Engineering and create or manage them as needed, so support teams have the reference material they need before launch.
Keep SOPs and SRMs current and findable, and use them to reduce repeat escalations.
Write knowledge articles and business process maps that let Tier-1/Tier-2 teams resolve issues without escalation.
Act as SME and point of contact for development and product partners.
Security, SOX & Compliance
Maintain compliance with security policies and change controls.
Support technology compliance activities, audit reporting, and SOX controls, and help close findings.
Follow the SDLC (Agile) and change, deployment, incident, and problem management processes.
Collaboration & Growth
Partner effectively with vendors, engineers, and business teams across time zones.
Mentor Systems Analysts and new joiners, and share knowledge through documentation and team forums.
Try new tools and practices, and bring ideas that improve how the team works.
Flexibility
On-call and travel as required, subject to local regulations. Other related duties as required.

0-3 years of hands-on platform or systems support, administration, or implementation experience in an enterprise IT environment.
Strong knowledge of Salesforce native functionality and best practices.
Demonstrated ability to manage escalations across teams and time zones, respond as a frontline responder in incidents (including knowing when to pull in reliability engineers), and own RCAs through resolution.
Experience with declarative tools (Flow, validation rules), data loading, and troubleshooting complex data and configuration issues.
Working knowledge of Service Management practices (incident, problem, change) and the SDLC.
Ability to design lightweight processes, SOPs, and reference manuals that others can run.
Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently in a distributed, global team.
Certifications (achieved): Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201), Advanced Administrator (ADM-211), and Platform App Builder. Platform Developer I achieved or actively pursuing.
Preferred
Certifications: Data 360, Tableau, or other specialist or consultant certifications.
Hands-on experience with Data 360, Agentforce, CRM Analytics, or Tableau.
Experience building monitors, alerts, or automation (observability tooling, Flow, scripting).
Intermediate coding (Apex, Python, SQL).

jobs.description:
About NCR Atleos
NCR Atleos, headquartered in Atlanta, is a leader in expanding financial access. Our dedicated 20,000 employees optimize the branch, improve operational efficiency and maximize self-service availability for financial institutions and retailers across the globe.
Title: Application Security Compliance Lead
Location: Gurgaon or Hyderabad, India
About NCR Atleos
NCR Atleos Corporation (NYSE: NATL) is a global technology company that enables financial access and commerce through assisted and self-service solutions and comprehensive support services. NCR Atleos serves financial and public-sector organizations in more than 100 countries and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
The opportunity
As an Application Security Compliance Lead, you will help ensure that NCR Atleos software products and development practices meet applicable security, privacy and regulatory requirements. Working within our global Application Security team, you will turn complex requirements into practical guidance, prepare teams for assessments, and help demonstrate that security and privacy are embedded throughout the software lifecycle.
A major focus is organization-level PCI Software Security Framework (SSF) activities: support product teams to achieve and retain PCI Secure Software Standard listings and maintain validation of our Secure Software Lifecycle practices. This role suits someone who combines compliance expertise with software development and application security knowledge.
What you will do
Govern the Secure SDLC. Maintain and improve practices aligned with the PCI Secure SLC Standard.
Enable PCI SSF validation. Guide teams through external assessment, self-assessment, annual attestation and periodic revalidation activities.
Interpret requirements. Translate security, privacy, legal and industry requirements into clear, proportionate guidance.
Assess readiness and close gaps. Coordinate reviews, evidence, gap analysis, remediation and resolution of findings.
Engage and influence. Partner with engineering, Legal, risk, compliance and security teams, QSAs and the PCI SSC.
Build capability. Create training and reusable guidance; monitor developments and communicate material changes.
Drive continual improvement. Use industry changes, stakeholder feedback, internal audits, assessment outcomes, recurring findings, and incidents to strengthen controls and processes.
What you will bring
Essential experience and capabilities
Typically, 7+ years of relevant experience in application security, software security assurance, secure software development, technology risk, privacy, compliance, or audit.
Practical experience developing, operating, governing or assessing a Secure SDLC.
Experience interpreting security or compliance requirements and supporting assessments, evidence collection, gap analysis and remediation.
Working knowledge of threat modelling, vulnerability management, security testing, and risk-based decision-making.
Technical understanding of cloud services, source-code management, and CI/CD practices sufficient to engage credibly with engineering teams.
Ability to convert complex requirements into pragmatic guidance and make evidence-based recommendations.
Strong stakeholder management, communication, analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority.
Ability to work independently and effectively within a globally distributed team.
Comfortable using AI assistants, such as Copilot, responsibly in day-to-day work to improve personal productivity, quality, and speed of delivery.
A bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience and qualifications.
Desirable experience and capabilities
Direct experience of PCI SSF validation or a comparable software security assurance framework.
Knowledge of payment-card security, GDPR requirements, NIST CSF and OWASP standards and guidance.
Experience delivering application security or compliance-related training.
Knowledge of security and governance for AI-enabled software development and products.
A relevant certification, such as CISSP, CSSLP, CIPP, CIPT or CIPM.
How you will succeed
Teams receive clear, timely, and actionable compliance guidance.
PCI SSF validation activities are well planned, appropriately evidenced, and progressed effectively.
Compliance gaps and findings are clearly owned, prioritized, tracked, and resolved.
Secure SDLC requirements remain practical, current, and consistently understood.
Assessment and incident lessons lead to sustainable improvements and strong stakeholder relationships.
Evidence we value
In your application, we would particularly welcome examples of how you have interpreted a security standard, prepared a product or organization for assessment, resolved a significant compliance gap, or influenced an engineering team to adopt a more effective security practice.

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As a Senior Product Manager for Data Integrations, you'll help GitLab's analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) agents see beyond the data held in GitLab. You'll decide which external systems connect to the Data Insights Platform and Orbit, which integrations come first, and how their data fits into shared models.
Engineering teams plan work, track incidents, monitor production, and manage security findings across different tools. Your challenge is to bring that context together with GitLab's code, merge requests, pipelines, deployments, and vulnerabilities. You'll shape a consistent approach that gives customers a trustworthy picture they can query, report on, and use with agents, rather than another set of disconnected data sources.
This role is based in Bangalore, India. You'll work from home and come to the Bangalore office when needed for business or team activities. You should be based in Bangalore or willing to relocate there.
What you'll do
Set integration priorities using evidence from customers, field teams, and other product managers to identify the biggest gaps in context.
Shape how external data maps into GitLab's shared data models, including the extract, transform, and load (ETL) approach and the transformations needed to make sources work together.
Define the customer problems and user groups each integration serves. Partner with engineering to agree on the intended experience, trade-offs, and delivery sequence.
Translate product decisions into a clear backlog of epics and issues for engineering.
Define telemetry and adoption signals to understand whether connected data helps customers answer new questions, and use those findings to guide priorities.
Help shape integration pricing and packaging as the product area matures.
Use AI coding agents and GitLab to explore data, prototype integrations, and document the intended experience.
What you'll bring
Product management experience, with the ability to connect customer needs to priorities and make trade-offs with incomplete information.
Strong knowledge of the software development and operations (DevOps) ecosystem, including how planning, security, observability, and IT service management tools fit into engineering workflows.
A working understanding of data integration, ETL, and data transformation, including how data from different systems maps to a common model. You don't need a background as a data engineer.
Comfort using AI tools for prototyping and documentation as part of your product work.
Clear communication about customer problems, close collaboration with engineering, and a habit of using data to evaluate adoption.
Experience with integration products, data models, or value stream analytics is helpful, but isn't required.
About the team
We're part of GitLab's Core Data Products organization, which focuses on insights, analytics, and data-driven decision-making. You'll report to the Vice President of Product Management and join as our third product manager, focused on Data Integrations. You'll work alongside a Principal Product Manager responsible for the Data Insights Platform and dashboards, and a Product Manager focused on Orbit.
GitLab is all-remote, with asynchronous collaboration across regions. Transparency, written communication, and clear decisions are central to how we work. This role has the Bangalore location and in-person requirements described above.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Subsystem Interoperability & AI-Driven Verification
jobs.description:
Job Title:
Staff Engineer - Subsystem Interoperability & AI-Driven Verification
Location- Bangalore
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You are a verification engineer who thinks in systems, across IP blocks. You understand where interoperability problems show up: architectural boundaries, configurations, initialization sequences, protocol interactions, firmware dependencies, clock and reset domains, implementation constraints, and assumptions made between independently developed IP. Deep hands-on verification skill sits alongside the judgment to shape methodology and influence interface and testbench decisions with partner teams. You are equally comfortable building a subsystem verification environment, reviewing SystemVerilog/UVM code, analyzing coverage, debugging a difficult Controller-PHY interaction in Verdi, writing Python automation, and explaining the technical tradeoff to architects and partner teams. You turn interoperability failures into subsystem fixes that prevent the same class of issue in later configurations. The hardest cross-IP investigations are the work you want, because a clear root cause becomes a test, a check, or a design change that protects customers. At Synopsys, you will verify subsystem interoperability across high-speed interface IPs, and you will apply GenAI, LLMs, and agentic workflows so qualification is continuous and backed by evidence.
What You'll Be Doing
Drive subsystem interoperability verification across Controller, PHY, firmware, VIP, verification environments, and customer configurations for one or more high-speed interface IP families
Design and build the verification content and flows for a scalable Interop Verification Platform: continuous integration, verification, and qualification across IP releases, covering the configuration space of Controller × PHY × Firmware × VIP × Protocol Mode × Customer Configuration, and using risk and coverage to decide what must be qualified
Develop reusable verification architectures, methodologies, and reference environments for functional verification, protocol compliance, error and stress scenarios, coverage, assertions, CDC/RDC, and system initialization
Own the hardest cross-IP investigations and drive fixes across RTL, PHY, firmware, VIP, testbench, and implementation boundaries when interoperability issues appear
Work with Controller and PHY architects and R&D teams early in the lifecycle on interfaces, observability, design-for-verification, and subsystem behavior
Apply GenAI, LLMs, RAG, and agentic workflows to the verification work this team owns, from specification and verification intent through environment, tests, regression, debug, qualification, and what the team learns from each failure
Build AI-assisted flows for environment and test generation, regression selection, log and failure clustering, coverage-gap analysis, protocol and waveform debug, root-cause recommendations, engineering knowledge retrieval, and qualification evidence
The Impact You Will Have
Make interoperability a continuous part of development for the subsystems you own, so bring-up and qualification start earlier and finish with evidence
Verify a growing set of IP configurations so Controller-PHY combinations are exercised before they reach a customer environment
Turn field and integration issues into permanent tests and shared debug knowledge, so the same failure does not return and the team keeps the lesson
Contribute reusable interoperability methods across the protocols you work on, including UCIe, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet, DDR/HBM, USB, and AMBA/CHI
Apply an AI-assisted verification flow so debug skill and methodology extend across more products and configurations
Produce compatibility matrices and qualification evidence that show when a specific Controller-PHY combination is ready for customers, and shorten integration time
Mentor other engineers and raise the quality of environments, reviews, and debug on the team
What You'll Need
5+ years of ASIC, IP, or SoC verification experience, with ownership of complex verification work and a record of influencing design and verification decisions with partner teams. Senior Staff candidates also show broader scope: reusable architectures or methodologies adopted beyond a single project, and technical leadership of interoperability work across configurations or teams
Deep expertise in SystemVerilog, UVM, assertions, functional and code coverage, verification closure, and complex debug, including building and reviewing sophisticated verification environments
Experience creating reusable verification environments for IP, subsystem, or SoC designs that other engineers could pick up and extend
Strong expertise in one or more high-speed protocols such as UCIe, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet, DDR/HBM, USB, or AMBA/CHI, including protocol interactions, initialization sequences, and interoperability issues
Hands-on use of industry simulation and debug tools, VIP, and coverage infrastructure, specifically VCS and Verdi or an equivalent toolchain
Automation skill in Python, Tcl, or a similar language, with examples of scripts or tools that made verification faster or more reliable
Experience with CDC/RDC, formal verification, emulation or prototyping, CI/CD, or distributed regression infrastructure is an advantage, as is experience or a demonstrated interest in GenAI, LLMs, RAG, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted verification
Who You Are
You can join a Controller-PHY integration that is failing in a customer configuration, debug the waveforms in Verdi, find the root cause across firmware, RTL, and protocol assumptions, and define the fix that prevents the same issue in later configurations
You align partner teams through technical credibility, clear communication, and a record of closing hard problems
You mentor other engineers by teaching them how to structure a verification environment and how to reason about a subsystem failure
You move between hands-on work and technical planning: reviewing a UVM testbench, proposing the verification approach for the next release, and walking architects through a risk in the interface or the initialization sequence
You treat AI and LLMs as practical tools for scaling verification, and you are ready to apply GenAI from specification through qualification on the work this team owns
You raise concerns when an interface creates interoperability risk or a qualification plan has no evidence behind it, because the subsystem has to work in the customer's configuration
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will work in the IP R&D organization at Synopsys with Controller and PHY architects, verification engineers, firmware engineers, and VIP developers across high-speed interface IP families. Your work sits where these teams meet: you own interoperability verification and help define the checks, environments, and evidence that show a subsystem works as a subsystem. You will collaborate with engineers in Bangalore and at other R&D sites. The role is hands-on and technical. Customer-ready Controller-PHY combinations depend on the quality of this work.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Memory Layout Design
jobs.description:
Memory Layout, Staff Engineer
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent years in the trenches of custom layout, and somewhere along the way you realized the real leverage is not in drawing one more SRAM cell, it is in building the frameworks that let hundreds of those cells get generated correctly, verified automatically, and scaled to the next node without reinventing everything. You think in systems, not schematics. When you look at a new process node, you are already mapping out the design rules, the automation gaps, and the verification bottlenecks before anyone asks.
You are the engineer who gets called when a layout flow breaks at 3nm or when a compiler needs to scale and no one is sure how to get StarRC and Custom Compiler to play nicely together. You do not just script solutions, you architect them with an eye toward maintainability, reuse, and the next three nodes. You have strong opinions about what good automation looks like, and you are not afraid to push back when a methodology does not serve the people who will actually use it.
At Synopsys, you will define how next-generation embedded memory gets built, not by drawing it yourself, but by creating the infrastructure that makes it possible for teams across the company to do it faster, cleaner, and more reliably.
What You'll Be Doing
Lead technology studies and process entitlement evaluations for advanced nodes (FinFET, GAA) to define what is physically possible and translate that into actionable layout guidelines for embedded memory compiler teams
Architect and build layout automation frameworks using Python and TCL that generate, verify, and validate custom memory IP layouts at scale, not one-off scripts but production infrastructure
Develop and maintain automated physical verification flows integrating Synopsys Custom Compiler, StarRC for parasitic extraction, and Ansys Totem for EM/IR reliability analysis across memory compiler products
Author and document physical implementation design rules, best practices, and layout methodologies that become the standard for how SRAM, ROM, and register file compilers are built and scaled
Evaluate next-generation EDA tools and capabilities, working directly with vendors and internal teams to define what gets adopted, how it gets integrated, and what productivity gains are realistic
Provide technical leadership and mentorship to layout development teams, troubleshooting complex verification failures, flow bottlenecks, and tool integration issues that block progress
Collaborate with foundry partners on design-technology co-optimization, feeding real-world layout constraints and automation needs back into process development discussions
The Impact You Will Have
Enable Synopsys memory compiler teams to scale to next-generation nodes faster by defining clear, automated methodologies that eliminate guesswork and rework
Reduce time-to-market for embedded memory IP by building verification and extraction flows that catch issues early and run without manual intervention
Improve layout productivity across the organization by delivering automation tools and infrastructure that teams actually use and trust
Influence foundry roadmaps and EDA tool development by representing real custom layout challenges and methodology needs in co-optimization discussions
Establish the technical standard for how advanced memory architectures are physically implemented, verified, and delivered at Synopsys
Mentor and elevate layout engineers by providing them with better tools, clearer guidelines, and a methodology framework that scales with their work
Drive reliability and quality improvements by automating EM/IR analysis and parasitic extraction in ways that surface problems before tapeout
What You'll Need
5+ years of hands-on experience in custom IC layout methodology, EDA automation, or physical design enablement, with a strong focus on embedded memory architectures like SRAM, ROM, or register files
Deep proficiency in Python and TCL for building production-grade layout automation tools, verification flows, and EDA infrastructure, not just scripting but software development
Extensive experience developing and deploying automated physical verification flows using Synopsys Custom Compiler, StarRC, Ansys Totem, or equivalent industry-standard tools
Solid understanding of advanced process nodes (FinFET, GAA, 5nm and below) and the ability to translate complex foundry design rules into engineering guidelines and automation requirements
Strong working knowledge of DRC/LVS/Antenna checking, EM/IR drop analysis, and parasitic extraction methodologies in the context of full-custom layout
Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or related field with a focus on EDA or layout methodology
Experience collaborating with foundry teams on design-technology co-optimization or familiarity with AI/ML frameworks for automating engineering tasks is a strong plus
Who You Are
You can walk into a room with a process design kit and walk out with a methodology roadmap that accounts for layout complexity, tool limitations, and team bandwidth
When a verification flow fails in a way no one has seen before, you do not escalate immediately, you dig into the tool logs, reproduce the issue, and figure out what broke and why
You write automation code that other engineers can actually read, maintain, and extend six months later without needing you to explain every function
You have a point of view on what good layout methodology looks like and you are comfortable defending it in a room full of senior engineers who may not agree
You can explain a complex tradeoff between layout density, verification runtime, and EM reliability to a product manager in two sentences without losing the technical nuance
You stay current on EDA tool capabilities, process technology trends, and automation techniques because you know that what worked at 7nm will not necessarily work at 3nm
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will join the Memory Layout Methodology and Automation team in Noida, a group responsible for defining how embedded memory compilers are physically implemented, verified, and scaled across Synopsys IP products. This is a technical leadership role where your work directly shapes the infrastructure and guidelines that memory development teams rely on to deliver next-generation SRAM, ROM, and register file IP to customers.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

The difference between a VCO that locks cleanly across PVT and one that drifts at the edge of spec is something you see coming three design reviews earlier, and you are the kind of engineer who catches it before it becomes a silicon problem. You think in both transistor-level trade-offs and team-level execution. When a junior designer brings you a sampler topology, you can spot the bandwidth bottleneck in two minutes and sketch three alternatives that might work better, then help them choose the right one for this particular standard and this particular process node.
Managing a team does not mean you stop designing. You still get into the schematics when a critical path needs attention, but you also know when to step back and let your team solve it. Lead a team of analog designers developing multi-Gbps NRZ and PAM4 SerDes IP from standards analysis through silicon bring-up
Conduct technical design reviews for critical SerDes sub-circuits including equalizers, samplers, voltage and current-mode drivers, serializers, deserializers, VCOs, phase mixers, DLLs, PLLs, bandgap references, ADCs, and DACs

Review simulation results, electrical characterization data, and post-silicon debug findings, then recommend design updates or corrective actions

Develop and mentor your team through hiring, technical coaching, design reviews, and career growth conversations
Work cross-functionally with digital designers, verification engineers, layout teams, and CAD to resolve mixed-signal integration and timing challenges

What You'll Need

14+ years of hands-on analog design experience focused on high-speed SerDes applications
1 to 2 years in a management or supervisory role leading analog design teams

Proven ability to design IP for high-speed connectivity standards such as PCIe and Ethernet
Solid understanding of mixed-signal design challenges including analog-digital interface timing, ESD circuit techniques and layout, custom digital design for high-speed logic paths, and layout effects like matching, reliability, and proximity

You stay technically hands-on even in a management role. You can still open a schematic, debug a phase noise issue, or review a layout for matching and reliability concerns without losing a step.

Agentic or RAG exposure: Built at least one working agent or retrieval pipeline end to end, with the ability to explain its design, failures and improvements.
Integration skills: Comfortable reading unfamiliar enterprise API documentation and determining how to integrate safely.
Version control and CI: Comfortable using Git in a team environment and working with automated build and test pipelines.
AI-assisted development: Daily working fluency with tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, with the judgement to critically review generated output.
Education: B.E./B.Tech/M.Tech in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Production agents: Experience deploying AI agents or LLM features into production, including multi-agent coordination or autonomous decision loops.
Enterprise application knowledge: Exposure to one or more of the following: Salesforce: REST/Composite/Bulk APIs, SOQL/SOSL, Connected Apps, OAuth and Apex. SAP: OData, BAPI/RFC, IDocs or business-object events. Enterprise platforms: AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning, Licensing/Entitlement or ITSM platforms and their supporting distributed services.
Vector databases and embeddings: Experience with semantic search, embedding generation and vector engines such as pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant or ChromaDB.
Advanced retrieval: Familiarity with Graph RAG, Corrective RAG, HyDE or agentic retrieval, and graph stores such as Apache AGE or Neo4j.
Model Context Protocol: Experience authoring MCP servers, including tools, resources and prompts.
Cloud and DevOps: Exposure to GCP, AWS or Azure, containerisation using Docker or Kubernetes, and serverless computing. Vertex AI experience is a plus.
Test automation: Familiarity with Playwright, REST Assured, Selenium or PyTest.

Join at the AI Engineer tier of the internal AI capability ladder, between AI User and AI Architect.
Progress towards AI Architect, building expertise in: Planner–executor orchestration at scale. Multi-agent systems with human-in-the-loop controls. Event-driven integration across enterprise IT systems. Model customisation.
Access company-funded training to support this progression.

Contribute to a people-centric culture focused on creating an exceptional employee experience.
Help expand what is possible in the workplace through innovation and collaboration

We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.

jobs.title: Layout Design Engineer, Sr Staff
jobs.description:
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent years in the trenches of full-custom analog layout, and you know that the difference between a SERDES block that closes timing and one that doesn't often comes down to a routing decision you made three weeks before tape-out. You think in layers, in parasitic budgets, in current density maps.
What You'll Be Doing
Own top-level layout integration for Analog/Mixed-Signal IP, driving floorplan optimization, block assembly, power distribution architecture, signal routing strategy, and full chip-level physical implementation from concept through tape-out
Drive Bump Map architecture and co-design with package teams, including signal and power bump assignment, ESD discharge path verification, IR-drop and current density analysis, substrate noise isolation strategy, and reliability validation
Develop full-custom layouts for high-speed SERDES blocks including TX/RX datapaths, PLL, VCO, LDO, Bandgap, Bias circuits, CTLE, VGA, and Clock Distribution Networks, optimizing for signal integrity, matching, area, and performance
Implement and validate layout techniques including differential routing with shielding, common-centroid and interdigitated device placement, symmetry-based matching structures, parasitic-aware routing, and ESD/latch-up mitigation
Execute physical verification and sign-off using Calibre DRC/LVS/ERC, ICV, StarRC/StarRCXT for extraction, PERC for parasitic analysis, and EMIR tools for electromigration and IR-drop validation
Mentor and technically develop junior layout engineers through structured design reviews, hands-on guidance on complex blocks, knowledge-sharing sessions on advanced layout techniques, and day-to-day problem-solving collaboration
Work directly with circuit designers, verification teams, and package engineers to resolve layout-driven performance issues, close timing on critical paths, and ensure manufacturability and reliability across advanced process nodes
The Impact You Will Have
Enable tape-out success for high-performance Analog IP that powers SERDES, AI, and compute products across Synopsys customer base by delivering layouts that meet aggressive PPA targets on the first pass
Reduce re-spin risk and schedule slip by catching EM, IR, signal integrity, and reliability issues early through disciplined physical verification and proactive collaboration with design and package teams
Accelerate layout closure timelines by building reusable floorplan templates, optimized routing strategies, and verified layout cells that can be leveraged across multiple IP variants and technology nodes
Strengthen the layout engineering capability of the Bangalore team by mentoring junior engineers, establishing best practices, and building institutional knowledge around advanced nodes like 5nm, 3nm, and Intel 18A
Improve cross-functional collaboration between layout, circuit design, and verification by translating complex parasitic and reliability constraints into actionable design guidance that circuit teams can use upstream
Contribute to Synopsys IP competitiveness by delivering layouts optimized for the latest FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAA) process technologies, enabling customers to achieve differentiated performance in their silicon
Drive quality and reliability outcomes by ensuring every layout you touch passes EM, IR, ESD, latch-up, and DRC/LVS clean on submission, reducing downstream verification cycles and freeing up team bandwidth for new development
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics Engineering, VLSI Design, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
8+ years of hands-on experience in full-custom Analog/Mixed-Signal CMOS layout design, with demonstrated ownership of blocks from floorplan through tape-out
Strong expertise in high-speed SERDES layout, including TX/RX datapaths, PLL, VCO, and clock distribution networks, with a track record of meeting timing, signal integrity, and performance targets
Proficiency in layout techniques including differential routing and shielding, common-centroid and interdigitated matching, symmetry-based placement, parasitic-aware routing, and ESD/latch-up mitigation strategies
Deep working knowledge of physical verification and sign-off flows using Calibre (DRC/LVS/ERC), ICV, StarRC or StarRCXT for extraction, PERC, and EMIR tools for electromigration and IR-drop analysis
Experience with Synopsys Custom Compiler or equivalent custom layout tools (Cadence Virtuoso, Mentor Pyxis), and comfort learning new toolsets as needed
Experience with advanced technology nodes such as 5nm, 3nm, Intel 18A/18AP, or equivalent FinFET/GAA processes is a strong plus, as is exposure to scripting with TCL, Perl, or Python for layout automation
Who You Are
You can look at a floorplan and immediately spot the routing bottleneck, the IR-drop risk, or the matching problem that will surface three weeks later, and you speak up before it becomes a schedule issue
You do not treat physical verification as a checkbox exercise. When an EM violation appears, you trace the current path, understand the circuit intent, and propose a fix that does not break something else downstream
You are comfortable sitting with a circuit designer who is frustrated about parasitic capacitance on a critical node and walking out with a routing plan that gives them the 50 femtofarads they need without blowing up area or DRC

Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process.
